title: Evidence terms: a check establishes one property, and is not read as another
note: The vocabulary is only useful while it is held to the code. The mutations that matter are the ones that would let a check be described as establishing more than it does: an implication added between independent properties, a historical name re-pinned to semantic support, or a registered check that no longer exists.

mutations.name: ET1_history_implies_the_world
mutations.rationale: a log that records a state would read as the world being in that state

mutations.name: ET2_verified_bytes_imply_support
mutations.rationale: a citation that resolves would read as one that supports the claim, which is the conflation the module exists to prevent

mutations.name: ET3_memory_evidence_key_repinned_to_support
mutations.rationale: the historical key would be described as establishing semantic support it never checks

mutations.name: ET4_registered_check_does_not_exist
mutations.rationale: the registry would describe a check the code does not have

mutations.name: ET5_a_check_disclaims_what_it_establishes
mutations.rationale: the gate would be recorded as not establishing the one property it does establish

mutations.name: ET6_an_assessed_check_backs_an_authority_decision
mutations.rationale: an authority decision would rest on a fallible judgement

mutations.name: ET7_a_history_check_establishes_the_world
mutations.rationale: a claim matching the reconstructed history would be reported as true of the world
